spray_brush_rate_check.notes: Spray rate >= brush rate on all 4 paired application tasks. PRIME_FRAME: spray(12) > brush(7). PRIME_SLAB: spray(10) > brush(4). FINISH_FRAME: spray(10) > brush(5). FINISH_SLAB: spray(8) > brush(3.5). Door spray IS faster than brush (opposite of wall spray/backroll coupling constraint — doors spray faster because spray eliminates brush marks on scrutinized surfaces).

doctrine_compliance.details: QT3 minimum enforced (no QT2). Door-specific QT modifiers: QT3=1.0, QT4=1.4, QT5=1.8 (higher than global). 3rd brush coat at QT5 per FFD 15.10.3. Hardware remove for spray, mask for brush per Section 10. Edge assigned to face per Section 10.3. Panel door sequencing (panels-rails-stiles) documented.

Interstage sanding at all tiers (QT3 spot 220, QT4 full 220, QT5 thorough 320). Rigid sanding block for flat surfaces (FFD 15.4.1). Apply-tip-walk-away protocol for waterborne products (FFD 15.3.1). Roll-and-tip option for flat frame surfaces (FFD 15.6). Fine-finish material systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5).

6 protection zones defined. Method-dependent protection: brush=perimeter drops + hardware mask, spray=8ft radius + wall mask + hardware remove. Glass masking for French doors. Teardown tasks paired with setup tasks.

Modifier stacking partition enforced: prep pool (condition x door_type x height) never includes QT; coating pool (QT x door_type x height) never includes condition. Worst-case flagged for estimator review when exceeding 4.0x threshold.

All required sections present: scope boundaries, configuration dimensions, paintable items, variants (to be created in spec.json), required PaintScope inputs, protection zones, adjacency declarations, state declarations, site condition rules.

State-driven primer selection. Shellac stain-blocker mandate for smoke damage (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT — no latex/acrylic alternative). CON_ prefix for all consumables. All consumable categories from controlled_enums.json.

warnings.message: Worst-case modifier stacking exceeds 4.0x for both pools when louvered door type is combined with extreme conditions. Prep: 6.50x (POOR x louvered x H2). Coating: 5.85x (QT5 x louvered x H2). These combinations are extremely rare in practice (louvered doors rarely get QT5 treatment, and tall louvered doors in POOR condition are uncommon).
warnings.recommendation: Production.json correctly flags these for estimator review. No action needed beyond documentation.

warnings.message: TSK_DIRP_FINISH_FRAME_ROLL_TIP is an alternative to TSK_DIRP_FINISH_FRAME_BRUSH (estimator selects one, not both). Both are included in SOP and production counts. This is correct — the estimator selects per project — but the alternative relationship should be clearly surfaced in spec.json variants.
warnings.recommendation: Document roll-and-tip as alternative in spec.json sequencing_notes.

warnings.message: Production.json condition_scale modifier on TSK_DIRP_DEGLOSS_FRAME and TSK_DIRP_DEGLOSS_SLAB includes GOOD/FAIR/POOR values, but these tasks have substrate_state_rules that skip them for SS_INT_PEELING/SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE/SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE (which map to POOR). The condition_scale modifier POOR value (2.0x) would only apply if the task were activated, which it is not for POOR states. This is not an error — the modifier is a rate adjustment only when the task is active — but could be confusing to implementers.
warnings.recommendation: Add a clarifying note in production.json rate_basis_notes that POOR modifier is defensive only.
